title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A Georgia couple lost approximately $800,000 to a cryptocurrency scam in which scammers used an AI-generated fake website to display false account balances. The deception began with an unsolicited WhatsApp message that led to a mobile trading app. The victims were initially allowed to make small trades and withdraw funds, which established false confidence in the platform's legitimacy.

The failure occurred at the point of account visibility. The scammers overlaid fabricated balance information on the victims' screens, showing money that did not exist. The couple discovered the fraud only when attempting a larger withdrawal. A human review of the actual account before processing a withdrawal, or independent verification of balance claims against the trading app's records, would have caught the deception before the loss occurred.

It is not established whether the trading app itself was compromised, whether the victims were targeted by name, or what specific AI techniques generated the fake website overlay.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway were convinced to invest through a mobile trading app that appeared legitimate, allowing them to make small trades and withdraw money initially, which built their trust. However, the scammers had created an AI-generated fake website that showed false investment balances on their screens, manipulating what Jerry could see in his account.

When Jerry tried to withdraw a larger amount last week, he discovered the money was gone and called police. Gwinnett County investigators confirmed the trading app was real but the scammers had created the fake overlay to deceive him. The couple is now speaking publicly to warn others about these sophisticated tactics. Police say victims in these cases rarely recover their funds. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help them with daily expenses while they work with law enforcement.
